chiefdom.name: Chiefdom
chiefdom.flavor: Whoever speaks last at the fire, speaks for all.
chiefdom.note: The chiefdom is what a people keep before they keep a law. It asks nothing of you and grants you nothing.

councilOfElders.name: Council of Elders
councilOfElders.flavor: Slow counsel, and no one hanged for it.
councilOfElders.text: +3 happiness. +1 renown per turn for each city you hold.

warChief.name: War Chief
warChief.flavor: The spear chooses; the rest agree.
warChief.text: +3 authority capacity. +4 combat strength. Killing a unit grants +5 science and +5 culture for each Order you have in a slot.

republic.name: Republic
republic.flavor: A crowd that learned to sign its name.
republic.text: +1 culture for each 5 population in a city. −5% happiness demanded per citizen.

tyranny.name: Tyranny
tyranny.flavor: One will, and the roads run straight.
tyranny.text: +5 authority capacity. +4 combat strength. Pillaging pays +50% and costs no movement.

theocracy.name: Theocracy
theocracy.flavor: Law is what the altar remembers.
theocracy.text: +2 faith in every city. Your capital's faith is gained again as science and as culture, at a fifth of the rate.

merchantLeague.name: Merchant League
merchantLeague.flavor: Every treaty has a ledger underneath.
merchantLeague.text: +2 gold for each economic Order you have in a slot · trade routes pay 50% more · +1 trade route.

imperium.name: Imperium
imperium.flavor: The map is a claim; the legion is the proof.
imperium.text: +1 production in every city for each military Order you have in a slot · all units +1 movement · capturing a city pays +50 gold and heals every one of your units.

divineMandate.name: Divine Mandate
divineMandate.text: +1 faith and +1 culture in your capital for each wildcard Order you have in a slot · +10% faith in every city of 6 or more population.
divineMandate.note: The tithe rises in your larger cities: nothing yet can ask whether a city is content.

theEstates.name: The Estates
theEstates.flavor: Three orders, one hall, and the hall keeps the minutes.
theEstates.text: +1 happiness in every city. +2 culture in every city of 8 or more population.

theSultanate.name: The Sultanate
theSultanate.flavor: The road is short for those the Sultan sends.
theSultanate.text: All units +1 movement, and cities put 25% more production behind units — a fifth off their price. Captured cities +10% science and +10% culture.

theCuria.name: The Curia
theCuria.flavor: What is written in the register is what heaven remembers.
theCuria.text: +6 faith for each Cathedral. Faith buildings supply science equal to their faith.

theCommonwealth.name: The Commonwealth
theCommonwealth.flavor: The estate is common; the ledger is not.
theCommonwealth.text: Great people may be bought with gold. Great-person improvements pay +50% more.

theEmpire.name: The Empire
theEmpire.flavor: One frontier, and it is wherever the last courier stopped.
theEmpire.text: +6 authority capacity. +2 combat strength for each great general you have earned this game.

theMagisterium.name: The Magisterium
theMagisterium.flavor: The Magister does not rule. He sets the rules.
theMagisterium.text: Every offer of every kind shows one more card. +3 renown per turn for each wonder you hold.

hermitCrown.name: The Hermit Crown
hermitCrown.flavor: A small kingdom, held entirely in one hand.
hermitCrown.text: While you hold at most 4 cities: +30% to every yield in your capital.

riverKings.name: River Kings
riverKings.flavor: The river gives; the dry land is told to be grateful.
riverKings.text: +30% food in every city on fresh water; −10% food and −10% production in every city without it.

woodwrights.name: The Woodwrights
woodwrights.flavor: A forest is a city that has not been felled yet.
woodwrights.text: Clearing a forest or jungle pays +100% and grants +10 culture.

greatLitany.name: The Great Litany
greatLitany.flavor: Say it every day and it becomes true.
greatLitany.text: +1 culture for each 3 faith you gain per turn.

greatWarringTribes.name: The Great Warring Tribes
greatWarringTribes.flavor: No writ runs faster than a horse.
greatWarringTribes.text: +10% production toward units. Captured cities pay +5 science and +5 culture per turn.
greatWarringTribes.note: The courthouse clause did nothing — there is no courthouse in the game — and is struck.

wolfMothersPact.name: Wolf-Mother's Pact
wolfMothersPact.flavor: We are not their prey. We are their kin, and they take their share.
wolfMothersPact.text: Barbarians you kill join you at full health.

athenaeumOfTheRoad.name: Athenaeum of the Road
athenaeumOfTheRoad.flavor: Everything found is kept. Everything kept is known.
athenaeumOfTheRoad.text: A ruin you claim pays every option instead of one.
athenaeumOfTheRoad.note: Retired: this Doctrine is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

foundersRoad.name: The Founders' Road
foundersRoad.flavor: The first stone of every town is a monument to the road that brought it.
foundersRoad.text: Newly founded cities are joined to your nearest city by road · +1 culture in every city.

foundersCharter.name: The Founders' Charter
foundersCharter.flavor: The charter is read aloud before the first stone is laid.
foundersCharter.text: +2 authority capacity · newly founded cities are founded with a Monument.

musesCall.name: The Muses' Call
musesCall.flavor: The nine came before the schools did, and were not asked for papers.
musesCall.text: Great people may be called before the technology that opens them. Adopting this calls one great person. Great-person improvements pay +1 production.
musesCall.note: Renown banks from the first turn whether or not anybody answers it. This opens the door early, and opens it with somebody already through.

thalassocracy.name: Thalassocracy
thalassocracy.flavor: Our borders are wherever the tide reaches.
thalassocracy.text: Coastal cities gain 10% of their food yield as production.

mountainHold.name: Mountain Hold
mountainHold.flavor: The peaks are a wall nobody had to build.
mountainHold.text: +15% production in every city with a mountain tile · +10 city defence there.
mountainHold.note: The mountain has to stand inside the city’s own borders. A peak the bounds have not reached yet shelters nobody.

theSacredPath.name: The Sacred Path
theSacredPath.flavor: The old road runs under the trees, and it was not we who laid it.
theSacredPath.text: +1 faith on every forest hex · +1 culture on every jungle hex.

burningWay.name: The Burning Way
burningWay.flavor: Ash is faster than a plough.
burningWay.text: Clearing a forest or jungle costs no worker charge.
burningWay.note: The axes are free, but the ground keeps no memory of the woods: land you have cleared pays what bare land pays.

breadAndCircuses.name: Bread and Circuses
breadAndCircuses.flavor: Feed them, amuse them, and they will sing for you.
breadAndCircuses.text: While your authority is positive: +2 happiness in every city of 6 or more population. −2 gold in every city, always.

theTithe.name: The Tithe
theTithe.flavor: A tenth of the harvest, and the gods keep the books.
theTithe.text: +1 gold for each faith you gain per turn.

divineInspiration.name: Divine Inspiration
divineInspiration.text: +1% science and +1% culture for each 200 banked faith.
divineInspiration.note: Retired: this Doctrine is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. Banked faith is meant to be spent, and a card that paid for hoarding it argued the other way.

ironPrice.name: The Iron Price
ironPrice.flavor: Every death a verse; every verse a debt paid.
ironPrice.text: Killing a unit grants +20 culture · pillaging pays double.

manifestOfTheSteppe.name: Manifest of the Steppe
manifestOfTheSteppe.flavor: The grass ends where the horses stop, and the horses do not stop.
manifestOfTheSteppe.text: Mounted units gain +1 movement. Pillaging pays double.

gildedCourt.name: The Gilded Court
gildedCourt.flavor: Gold on the walls, gold in the words, gold under the throne.
gildedCourt.text: Unlocks the Gilded Hall, a building that is bought with gold and never built. +1 science and +1 culture on every hex that yields gold. +2 authority capacity.

grandBazaar.name: The Grand Bazaar
grandBazaar.flavor: The second silk is not nothing. The tenth is a fortune.
grandBazaar.text: Happiness from unique luxuries +50%. A second or later copy of a luxury pays 30% of its bonus instead of nothing. +2 gold for each unique luxury.

masterOfMaps.name: Master of Maps
masterOfMaps.flavor: We see everything. We fear it a little.
masterOfMaps.text: All units +1 sight and +1 movement, all units −4 combat strength.

hegemony.name: Hegemony
hegemony.flavor: Every city carries its own weight, and the crown carries none.
hegemony.text: A captured city costs 1 authority · capturing a city grants +5% production in every city for 10 turns.
hegemony.note: A city you take costs one authority — the least any law can make it.

paxImperia.name: Pax Imperia
paxImperia.flavor: In great cities the noise itself is a kind of peace.
paxImperia.text: +3 happiness and +10% culture in every city of 8 or more population.

religiousMandate.name: Religious Mandate
religiousMandate.flavor: There is one truth, and we are its army.
religiousMandate.text: Permanent war with empires of a different majority religion · your cities cannot be converted.
religiousMandate.note: Withdrawn until there is a war a faith can declare and a city a faith can hold shut. The row is kept so a saved game that already holds it keeps it.
deferred: permanent war with empires of another faith
a powerful bonus toward the domination and religious beads

theAcademyOfDeeds.name: The Academy
theAcademyOfDeeds.flavor: A deed unrecorded is a deed undone.
theAcademyOfDeeds.text: −10% culture and +20% science. Great scholar drafts can be bought with faith.

theStandingArmy.name: The Standing Army
theStandingArmy.flavor: The army does not go home. That is the whole of the doctrine.
theStandingArmy.text: +1 authority capacity for each 5 units you have in the field. −1 happiness in every city. Units cost no upkeep.

theSeaCharter.name: The Merchant Scholars
theSeaCharter.flavor: The ledger travels with the caravan and comes home the fuller of the two.
theSeaCharter.text: +2% science and +2% culture in every city for each trade route you run.

theRenaissanceCourt.name: The Renaissance Court
theRenaissanceCourt.flavor: Patronage is the cheapest thing a prince ever bought.
theRenaissanceCourt.text: Great-person offers show one more card.
theRenaissanceCourt.note: The clause about stronger legacies is struck: nothing makes a legacy stronger.

cuiusRegio.name: Cuius Regio
cuiusRegio.flavor: Whose realm, his religion; whose religion, his realm.
cuiusRegio.text: In cities that follow your religion, 15% of the faith they gain is gained again as science.

theYeomanry.name: The Yeomanry
theYeomanry.flavor: A man with forty acres argues with the tax collector.
theYeomanry.text: +1 production on every hex with a Farm. Cities of 10 or more population −1 happiness.

absolutism.name: Absolutism
absolutism.flavor: The council still meets. It meets to agree.
absolutism.text: +6 authority capacity. A newly placed Order is locked for 10 turns instead of 5.

blitz.name: Blitz
blitz.flavor: Stop only when there is nothing left in front of you.
blitz.text: Units that kill may move again that turn. Units cannot fortify.

thePhilosophersStone.name: The Philosopher's Stone
thePhilosophersStone.flavor: Lead is only gold that has not been asked properly.
thePhilosophersStone.text: The Magnum Opus is built 25% faster.
thePhilosophersStone.note: The clause about distilleries is struck: there is no distillery in the game.

theGrandTourII.name: The Grand Tour
theGrandTourII.flavor: One goes to see them, and comes back having been seen.
theGrandTourII.text: +3 renown per turn for each wonder you hold. +1 culture for each wonder in the world, seen or not.

mareNostrum.name: Mare Nostrum
mareNostrum.flavor: They call it a sea. We call it the middle of the country.
mareNostrum.text: +1 food and +2 gold on every water hex you own. +15% science in coastal cities.

theLeveeEnMasse.name: The Levée en Masse
theLeveeEnMasse.flavor: Every hearth owes a son, and the ledger remembers which.
theLeveeEnMasse.text: Every 10 turns, a free melee unit musters in your capital. It moves one further for the rest of the game.
theLeveeEnMasse.note: Every hearth owes a soldier, and the ones it sends march quicker than the men they replace.

paxMagistri.name: Pax Magistri
paxMagistri.flavor: The long quiet, and the accounts that grew in it.
paxMagistri.text: +3 happiness in every city. +5 science and +5 culture in every city of 12 or more population.

theEncyclopaedia.name: The Encyclopaedia
theEncyclopaedia.flavor: Everything, in order, by somebody who never left the room.
theEncyclopaedia.text: +1 science for each building in a city. Science buildings cost −50% production.

theGentleYoke.name: The Gentle Yoke
theGentleYoke.flavor: Ask little of them and they will not notice the asking.
theGentleYoke.text: −15% happiness demanded per citizen · every city costs 2 more authority.
theGentleYoke.note: The extra authority is asked of every city you hold, however long you have held it.

theScatteredHearths.name: The Scattered Hearths
theScatteredHearths.flavor: A hamlet of three keeps itself. A capital of thirty does not.
theScatteredHearths.text: The first 2 citizens in every city demand no happiness · −4 happiness in your capital.

theWanderingCourt.name: The Wandering Court
theWanderingCourt.flavor: The court sleeps where it stops, and the country is the better for it.
theWanderingCourt.text: −15% to every yield in your capital · +3 food, production, science, culture and faith, and +3 happiness, in every city but your capital.

thePilgrimWays.name: The Pilgrim Ways
thePilgrimWays.flavor: Every road that ends at an altar is a road somebody paid for.
thePilgrimWays.text: +3 faith for each city in the world that follows your religion · +1 culture for each foreign city that follows you · +1 culture for each 5 faith you gain per turn.
thePilgrimWays.note: Nothing yet marks the turn a city changes its faith, so the foreign congregation is counted rather than paid for at the moment it is won.

theNaturalPhilosophers.name: The Natural Philosophers
theNaturalPhilosophers.flavor: They measured the tower's shadow, and then they measured the tower.
theNaturalPhilosophers.text: +1 science in your capital for each building standing in it · completing a technology grants 50% of a turn’s culture.

theDeepDelving.name: The Deep Delving
theDeepDelving.flavor: The hill kept its secret for an age. It kept it badly.
theDeepDelving.text: +1 production on every mine and every quarry · surfacing a vein pays +40 gold, and a mine standing on rich ore pays +2 production more.

theClosedRealm.name: The Closed Realm
theClosedRealm.flavor: The gate is shut. What is inside it is enough.
theClosedRealm.text: Your happiness is fixed at +5, always · your units cannot attack outside your territory.
deferred: your happiness is held at +5 whatever your cities ask for
your units cannot attack outside your own territory
theClosedRealm.note: Not built, both halves. Nothing in this game can hold a meter at a number instead of adding to it, and nothing can refuse an attack for where it is being made.

theTriumphalWay.name: The Triumphal Way
theTriumphalWay.flavor: The road into the city was widened once, for one afternoon, four hundred years ago.
theTriumphalWay.text: Capturing a city grants +5 happiness in every city for 10 turns.

theHorseTribes.name: The Horse-Tribes
theHorseTribes.flavor: They were never conquered. They were hired.
theHorseTribes.text: Mounted units gain +1 movement and +2 combat strength.

bloodedSpears.name: Blooded Spears
bloodedSpears.flavor: The wild taught us. We took notes.
bloodedSpears.text: +2 combat strength, and +4 more against barbarians.

campFollowers.name: Camp Followers
campFollowers.text: Clearing a barbarian camp grants +25 food and a random military unit.

farRunners.name: Far Runners
farRunners.flavor: Run until the land is new, then run once more.
farRunners.text: All your units gain +1 sight. Claiming a ruin grants +10 culture.

theLongWatch.name: Martial Law
theLongWatch.flavor: The garrison is the government, and the town sleeps for it.
theLongWatch.text: +1 happiness for each military unit standing in one of your cities, and +1 more for each fortification a city has built.

theWidowsLevy.name: The Widow's Levy
theWidowsLevy.text: When a unit of yours dies, its nearest city gains +10 production and you gain +40 gold.

militiaLevies.name: Militia Levies
militiaLevies.flavor: Every farmer a spear, every roof a watchtower.
militiaLevies.text: All your cities gain +4 defense and +1 sight radius.
militiaLevies.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The wild is answered by soldiers, not by a flat on every wall.

commonGranary.name: Common Granary
commonGranary.flavor: One store, one hunger, one answer.
commonGranary.text: +2 food in every city holding an improved luxury resource.

saltTithes.name: Salt Tithes
saltTithes.flavor: Salt is small. Its tax is not.

boundaryStones.name: Boundary Stones
boundaryStones.flavor: A stone that says *ours* says it forever.
boundaryStones.text: +30% border expansion in every city with a Monument.
boundaryStones.note: Border expansion is how fast a city claims its next hex, fed by that city’s own culture — separate from the culture your empire saves toward its next draft. This hurries the borders only.

firstRites.name: First Rites
firstRites.text: +1 faith in your capital, and +1 faith for each wildcard Order you have in a slot.

borderBallads.name: Border Ballads
borderBallads.flavor: Fear, set to a tune, becomes a people.
borderBallads.text: +2 culture for each barbarian camp you have found, and +10 culture for each barbarian unit you kill.
borderBallads.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

borderWardens.name: Border Wardens
borderWardens.flavor: Home ground fights beside you — and fights harder the more of us there are.
borderWardens.text: +2 combat strength inside your territory, and +2 more for each military Order you have in a slot, at most +6 more.

vanguard.name: Vanguard
vanguard.flavor: Strangers' ground fights harder — so must we.
vanguard.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. Border Wardens stands in its place, and grows with the war cards beside it.

conscription.name: Conscription
conscription.note: The unhappiness is a flat charge on the realm, not a charge per city: nothing can count only the cities past a fourth one.

spoilsOfTheWild.name: Spoils of the Wild
spoilsOfTheWild.flavor: Their plunder was ours all along.
spoilsOfTheWild.note: It adds to Camp Followers rather than replacing it: a camp cleared under both pays both.

horseLords.name: Horse Lords
horseLords.flavor: The saddle is a country of its own.
horseLords.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The Horse-Tribes carries the mounted line now.

weightsAndMeasures.name: Weights & Measures
weightsAndMeasures.flavor: An honest scale is the first tax.

silkRoads.name: Silk Roads
silkRoads.flavor: Rare things travel; travel makes them rarer.
silkRoads.text: +5 gold on every trade route you run.
silkRoads.note: The coin rides on the road itself, so anything that raises what a route pays raises this with it.

theSaltRoad.name: The Salt Road
theSaltRoad.flavor: Every field pays a toll on its way to market.
theSaltRoad.text: +1 gold on every hex carrying a strategic resource.
theSaltRoad.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The Golden Scales stands in its place.

theTaxFarm.name: The Tax Farm
theTaxFarm.flavor: Count the people, and the coin counts itself.
theTaxFarm.text: +1 gold for each 3 population in your empire.

harbourDues.name: Harbour Dues
harbourDues.flavor: The sea pays for the privilege of arriving.
harbourDues.text: Coastal cities gain 5% of their gold again as culture.

landGrants.name: Land Grants
landGrants.flavor: Land, given freely, is land that was owed.
landGrants.text: Buying a hex costs 25% less · +40% border expansion.
landGrants.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. Royal Surveyors stands in its place.

homesteadCharters.name: Homestead Charters
homesteadCharters.flavor: The wagon holds one more family than the law allows.
homesteadCharters.text: Newly founded cities start with 1 more population.

granaryLevies.name: Granary Levies
granaryLevies.flavor: A new mouth is a new pair of hands.
granaryLevies.text: When a city grows, it gains +10 production.

censusRolls.name: The King's Table
censusRolls.flavor: A place is laid for every mouth in the city, and every mouth knows it.
censusRolls.text: +1 happiness for every 2 citizens in your capital.

tinkersGuild.name: Tinkers' Guild
tinkersGuild.flavor: One more mend in every bag of tools.

publicGranaries.name: Public Granaries
publicGranaries.flavor: The city eats slowly, and stays fed.
publicGranaries.text: Cities keep 15% of their stored food when they grow.
publicGranaries.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

festivalDays.name: Festival Days
festivalDays.flavor: Idleness, made sacred, keeps the peace.
festivalDays.text: +4 happiness in your capital, and +2 culture in every city.

curiousElders.name: Curious Elders
curiousElders.flavor: The old ask questions the young forgot to.
curiousElders.text: +5 science whenever you claim a ruin.
curiousElders.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

ritesOfPassage.name: Rites of Passage
ritesOfPassage.flavor: A sword blessed is a soul enlisted.
ritesOfPassage.text: Buying or completing a unit grants +10 faith.
ritesOfPassage.note: A unit bought with gold counts as completed, so it pays this too — but only once.

theLooseRein.name: The Loose Rein
theLooseRein.flavor: Laws that change quickly are laws that are watched closely.
theLooseRein.text: A newly placed Order is locked for 2 turns instead of 5.
theLooseRein.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

fieldSurgeons.name: Field Surgeons
fieldSurgeons.flavor: Stitched on the road, marching by morning.
fieldSurgeons.text: All units heal +10 more per turn, anywhere.

theShieldWall.name: The Shield Wall
theShieldWall.flavor: High ground and a locked line — the old arithmetic.
theShieldWall.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. Hill Forts stands in its place.

siegeDoctrine.name: Siege Doctrine
siegeDoctrine.flavor: Walls are patient. We are less so.

scorchedEarth.name: Scorched Earth
scorchedEarth.flavor: What we cannot keep, we salt.
scorchedEarth.text: Pillaging heals a further 25 and pays a further +10 gold.

sumptuaryLaws.name: Sumptuary Laws
sumptuaryLaws.flavor: Only the crown wears the purple; all the rest are glad to see it.

publicani.name: Publicani
publicani.flavor: The writ has a price, and we collect it.
publicani.text: +2 gold for each point of positive authority.
publicani.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

charteredCompanies.name: Chartered Companies
charteredCompanies.flavor: Every deed of land comes with a survey attached.
charteredCompanies.text: Buying a hex pays +5 science · buying a hex costs 15% less.

foreignQuarters.name: Foreign Quarters
foreignQuarters.flavor: The neighbour's coin spends as well as ours.
foreignQuarters.text: +1 gold and +1 science in every city near another empire's territory.
foreignQuarters.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

oreTithes.name: Ore Tithes
oreTithes.flavor: Where the ore is, the hammers gather.
oreTithes.text: +2 production on every hex carrying a strategic resource, and +2 production in your capital for each military Order you have in a slot.

terracedHillsides.name: Terraced Hillsides
terracedHillsides.flavor: The hill was made to feed us; it only needed steps.

masterMasons.name: Master Masons
masterMasons.flavor: Every finished wall is a song about itself.

royalSurveyors.name: Royal Surveyors
royalSurveyors.flavor: The chain and the plumb line, quietly annexing.
royalSurveyors.text: +50% border expansion · buying a hex costs 25% less.

provincialGovernors.name: Provincial Governors
provincialGovernors.flavor: Distance obeys, if someone is paid to make it.
provincialGovernors.text: +1 authority capacity for each economic Order you have in a slot, at most +4.

emergencyPowers.name: Emergency Powers
emergencyPowers.flavor: When the writ tears, the capital holds the pieces.
emergencyPowers.text: While your authority is negative: capital +25% production, and borders do not freeze.

theCommonPurse.name: The Common Purse
theCommonPurse.flavor: Nothing left on the workbench is wasted.
theCommonPurse.text: Leftover production from a completed item is doubled.
theCommonPurse.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

pilgrimRoads.name: Pilgrim Roads
pilgrimRoads.flavor: Where the faithful walk, the faithful settle.
pilgrimRoads.text: +1 faith for each citizen in your capital · +1 happiness for each 50 banked faith (at most +5).

lamplighters.name: Lamplighters
lamplighters.flavor: A small flame kept is a small song sung.
lamplighters.text: +1 culture for each 3 faith you gain per turn.

scholarsStipend.name: Scholars' Stipend
scholarsStipend.flavor: A crowd is a library that has not been catalogued.
scholarsStipend.text: +3 science in every city of 5 or more population holding a Library, and +3 more where a University stands.

theMarshals.name: The Marshals
theMarshals.flavor: Shoulder to shoulder, the line is one animal.
theMarshals.text: +4 combat strength for each adjacent friendly combat unit (at most +8).

garrisonState.name: Garrison State
garrisonState.flavor: The soldiers do not idle. Nobody does.
garrisonState.text: Each city gains +3 production for each combat unit standing in it (at most +6 per city).
garrisonState.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

skirmishersCreed.name: Skirmishers' Creed
skirmishersCreed.flavor: Strike from where they cannot answer.

theFinishersArt.name: The Finisher's Art
theFinishersArt.text: +4 combat strength against units below half strength.
theFinishersArt.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. Decisive Blows says the same rule, and says it bigger.

frontierForts.name: Frontier Forts
frontierForts.flavor: The border is where we keep our walls.
frontierForts.text: +6 city defence in every city near another empire's territory.
frontierForts.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

triumphs.name: Triumphs
triumphs.flavor: A city taken is a story told forever.
triumphs.text: Capturing a city grants +30 culture and +25 renown.
triumphs.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theStandingLevy.name: The Standing Levy
theStandingLevy.flavor: The spear is always first in line.
theStandingLevy.text: Every 12 turns, a free melee unit musters in your capital.

clientKings.name: Client Kings
clientKings.flavor: Better a king who bows than a province that rebels.
clientKings.text: +4 authority capacity · a captured city costs one less authority.

provincialMints.name: Provincial Mints
provincialMints.flavor: Every seam of silk, its own small coin.
provincialMints.text: +10% gold in every city holding an improved luxury resource.

quarrymensGuild.name: Quarrymen's Guild
quarrymensGuild.text: +4 production in every city with a quarry, and +1 production on every quarry.

theGrainDole.name: The Grain Dole
theGrainDole.flavor: A full city is a quiet one.
theGrainDole.text: +2 happiness in every city of 6 or more population.

mandateOfHeaven.name: Mandate of Heaven
mandateOfHeaven.flavor: The pious are easy to govern, and they know it.
mandateOfHeaven.text: The science and culture your happy cities pay rises 8 percentage points · +1 happiness for each 150 banked faith.

theLyceum.name: The Lyceum
theLyceum.flavor: Every new thing learned is a song about the old.
theLyceum.text: Completing a technology grants an extra turn of culture.

censusOfSouls.name: Census of Souls
censusOfSouls.flavor: A great city prays in a great voice.
censusOfSouls.text: +1 faith for each citizen in your capital.

tolerationEdicts.name: Toleration Edicts
tolerationEdicts.flavor: Let them keep their gods; they will pay their taxes.

theLaureate.name: The Laureate
theLaureate.flavor: The court keeps one chair empty, and it is never empty for long.
theLaureate.text: +2 renown per turn. Every great-person improvement pays +3 more of its own yield.
theLaureate.note: The great-person improvements are the academy, landmark, manufactory, customs house and citadel.

theLegion.name: The Legion
theLegion.flavor: Ten thousand men who march as one, and dig the ditch as one.
theLegion.text: Melee units gain +1 movement and +2 combat strength, and cities put 15% more production behind them.

fireKeepers.name: Fire-Keepers
fireKeepers.flavor: Someone has sat up with it every night since the first night.
fireKeepers.text: +1 faith in your capital for every 2 citizens living there.
fireKeepers.note: The faith is paid in your capital, so anything that raises what your capital receives raises this with it.

wolfRunners.name: Wolf-Runners
wolfRunners.flavor: They come back with the country in their heads.
wolfRunners.text: Scouts gain +1 movement, and claiming a ruin grants +15 gold.
wolfRunners.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

hearthSongs.name: Hearth Songs
hearthSongs.flavor: Small places keep the tunes the big ones forget.
hearthSongs.text: +2 culture in every city of 4 population or less.
hearthSongs.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The Harvest Songs stands in its place.

firstFruitsOffering.name: First Fruits
firstFruitsOffering.flavor: The first child of the season is carried to the stone, and given back.
firstFruitsOffering.text: The first citizen born in each city pays +10 faith once.
firstFruitsOffering.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. A tithe on a town’s first citizen pays nothing once the towns are grown.

statuteLabour.name: Statute Labour
statuteLabour.flavor: Every third back is owed to the road.
statuteLabour.text: +1 production in every city for each 4 citizens living there.
statuteLabour.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

riverWardens.name: River Wardens
riverWardens.flavor: The water is watched, so the water is shared.
riverWardens.text: +1 food on every farm beside fresh water.
riverWardens.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The waterworks of the tree already water a farm beside fresh water.

theAlmanac.name: The Almanac
theAlmanac.flavor: A year written down is a year that can be argued with.
theAlmanac.text: +2 science in your capital, and +2 science in every city with a Library.

villageFairs.name: Village Fairs
villageFairs.flavor: What the second cart carries is bought for pleasure.
villageFairs.text: +1 happiness for each luxury you hold two or more copies of.

theMusterRoll.name: The Muster Roll
theMusterRoll.flavor: The name is written before the man is asked.
theMusterRoll.text: Units created from now on are born with +10 maximum health, and keep it for life.
theMusterRoll.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. Drums of War stands in its place.

hillForts.name: Hill Forts
hillForts.flavor: Uphill, every stone is a soldier.
hillForts.text: +4 combat strength when defending on hills, and a city on hills costs 1 less authority.

thePilgrimsPurse.name: The Pilgrim's Purse
thePilgrimsPurse.flavor: Nobody walks that far without stopping to eat.
thePilgrimsPurse.text: +5 faith in every city standing beside a holy site.
thePilgrimsPurse.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

charterTowns.name: Charter Towns
charterTowns.flavor: The grain store is written into the charter, above the wall.
charterTowns.text: Newly founded cities are founded with a Granary.
charterTowns.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. Homestead Charters already founds a town better than it was founded.

theChoir.name: The Choir
theChoir.flavor: Forty voices, and not one of them heard on its own.
theChoir.text: +3 culture and +1 happiness in every city with a Temple.

starGazers.name: Star-Gazers
starGazers.flavor: Above the smoke, the sky keeps better records.
starGazers.text: +15% science in every city with a mountain hex inside its borders.

cisternWorks.name: Cistern Works
cisternWorks.flavor: The rain of one winter, kept under the square.
cisternWorks.text: Every city of yours counts as standing on fresh water.
cisternWorks.note: It answers what is asked of a city — whether the town can drink. A hex out in the fields is still watered by the river or by nothing.

ledgerKeepers.name: Ledger-Keepers
ledgerKeepers.flavor: The column of figures is longer than the road.
ledgerKeepers.text: +1 science and +1 culture on every trade route sent from a city with a Market, and +1 trade route.
ledgerKeepers.note: A road is read from the town that sent the caravan, so a Market at the far end of it pays nothing here.

drumsOfWar.name: Drums of War
drumsOfWar.flavor: They learn the step before they learn the spear.
drumsOfWar.text: While this Order is in a slot, units created from now on are born with +4 combat strength, and keep it for life.

theCartographers.name: The Cartographers
theCartographers.flavor: The blank part of the sheet is the part worth paying for.
theCartographers.text: +1 science for each 40 hexes you have revealed.

theMasonsLodge.name: The Masons' Lodge
theMasonsLodge.flavor: A trade that will not teach a stranger keeps its walls straight.
theMasonsLodge.text: Cities of 6 population or more put 10% more production behind buildings.
theMasonsLodge.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theOathBound.name: The Oath-Bound
theOathBound.flavor: They swore it over a fire, and the fire is still lit.
theOathBound.text: Killing a unit heals the unit that struck the blow by 15.

sanctuary.name: Sanctuary
sanctuary.flavor: They may take the gate, the granary and the gold. Not the stones.
sanctuary.text: Your holy city cannot be taken while it keeps your religion — it is sacked instead.
sanctuary.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. A city can only be taken in this game, never sacked, so nothing was left to keep.

waysideShrines.name: Wayside Shrines
waysideShrines.flavor: A stone, a bowl, a name. No priest required.
waysideShrines.text: +1 faith in your capital for every city you hold.
waysideShrines.note: The faith is gathered in your capital, so anything that raises what your capital receives raises this with it.

theOrchardTithe.name: The Orchard Tithe
theOrchardTithe.flavor: The tenth basket goes to the crown, and the crown plants it.
theOrchardTithe.text: +2 food on every hex carrying a luxury resource.

theUnbrokenLand.name: The Unbroken Land
theUnbrokenLand.flavor: Nothing was asked of this ground. It gave anyway.
theUnbrokenLand.text: +1 food and +1 production on every unimproved forest or jungle hex.

theGreenwoodLaw.name: The Greenwood Law
theGreenwoodLaw.flavor: The law of the greenwood is short enough to remember: leave it be.
theGreenwoodLaw.text: +2 food and +2 production on every unimproved hex.
theGreenwoodLaw.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theQuietFields.name: The Quiet Fields
theQuietFields.flavor: No plough, no boundary, no quarrel.
theQuietFields.text: +1 happiness for each unimproved hex your cities work.
theQuietFields.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. It paid a wide realm far more happiness than any other card of its age.

theOldWays.name: The Old Ways
theOldWays.flavor: They farmed here once. It has been better since they stopped.
theOldWays.text: The yields of unimproved hexes are doubled.

firstFruits.name: First Fruits
firstFruits.flavor: The first of everything is set aside. The rest feeds us.
firstFruits.text: +1 food and +1 gold on every hex carrying a resource.

theQuartermasters.name: The Quartermasters
theQuartermasters.flavor: An army marches on ledgers. The ledgers march on nothing at all.
theQuartermasters.text: Military units cost 1 less gold in maintenance.
theQuartermasters.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The War Chest stands in its place.

theWarChest.name: The War Chest
theWarChest.flavor: Kept locked, kept counted, kept full. Kept, above all.
theWarChest.text: Military units cost 2 less gold in maintenance.

forcedMarches.name: Forced Marches
forcedMarches.flavor: Sleep is a thing that happens to other armies.
forcedMarches.text: Melee units gain +1 movement, and +2 instead inside your own territory.

theEscortedRoads.name: The Escorted Roads
theEscortedRoads.flavor: The merchants pay for the spears, and the spears pay them back in miles.
theEscortedRoads.note: The escort is paid for in coin and not in safety: a route this law enriches can still be plundered.

theLastHunt.name: The Last Hunt
theLastHunt.flavor: They sing the old raids now. Nobody living remembers being afraid.
theLastHunt.text: +4 culture and +4 science for each barbarian camp you have cleared this game.

theSaintsFields.name: The Saints' Fields
theSaintsFields.flavor: Where a great one stopped to think, the ground has been holy ever since.
theSaintsFields.note: The great-person improvements are the academy, landmark, manufactory, customs house and citadel.

theWayhouses.name: The Wayhouses
theWayhouses.flavor: A bed, a fire, and somebody who will listen to where you have been.
theWayhouses.text: +1 gold and +3 culture for each trade route you run.

theProvisioners.name: The Provisioners
theProvisioners.flavor: Nobody notices the grain until the week it does not come.
theProvisioners.text: +1 happiness for each trade route between your own cities.

thePrizeGrounds.name: The Prize Grounds
thePrizeGrounds.flavor: They founded it on the vein and argued about the name for a century.
thePrizeGrounds.text: +2 happiness in every city settled on a luxury resource.
thePrizeGrounds.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theCensusEternal.name: The Census Eternal
theCensusEternal.flavor: Every soul written down, every year, for ever. The writing is the point.
theCensusEternal.text: +1 science for every 2 citizens in your empire.

theGroundskeepers.name: The Groundskeepers
theGroundskeepers.flavor: Someone has to weed around the monument.
theGroundskeepers.text: +2 food and +2 production on every great-person improvement.
theGroundskeepers.note: The great-person improvements are the academy, landmark, manufactory, customs house and citadel.

theMastersPresence.name: The Master's Presence
theMastersPresence.flavor: He is not often at home. The town works harder anyway, in case.
theMastersPresence.text: +15% to every yield in each city beside a great person’s work.
theMastersPresence.note: A city is beside a work when one stands on its own hex or on one of the six touching it. Two works never pay twice.

theWonderFeasts.name: The Wonder-Feasts
theWonderFeasts.flavor: The scaffolding goes up and the ovens do not go out again for a year.
theWonderFeasts.text: +4 food in every city while it is building a wonder · +20% production toward wonders.

theMasterBuilders.name: The Master Builders
theMasterBuilders.flavor: They have built one of everything. The second is always cheaper.
theMasterBuilders.text: The Magnum Opus and cathedrals cost 25% less production.

theShipwrightShores.name: The Shipwright Shores
theShipwrightShores.flavor: A town that smells of pitch is a town with somewhere to be.
theShipwrightShores.text: +3 production in every coastal city · +30% production toward ships there.

theDryDocks.name: The Dry Docks
theDryDocks.flavor: Pull the sea out from under her and you can see what she has been hiding.
theDryDocks.text: +25% production toward ships in every city with a Harbour.
theDryDocks.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theWinteringGrounds.name: The Wintering Grounds
theWinteringGrounds.flavor: Home is wherever the horses have stopped.
theWinteringGrounds.text: Your units cost no gold in maintenance outside your territory.
theWinteringGrounds.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The War Chest is the card that pays an army’s keep.

theArchives.name: The Archives
theArchives.flavor: Every law ever passed, in order, in a room nobody is allowed to leave.
theArchives.text: +2 culture for each Order you have placed in a slot.

theAnnalsOfLaw.name: The Annals of Law
theAnnalsOfLaw.flavor: The laws you chose not to pass are also history.
theAnnalsOfLaw.text: +3 culture for each Order you hold but have not placed in a slot.

theAuspiciousSeal.name: The Auspicious Seal
theAuspiciousSeal.flavor: The clerk who chose the day was promoted, and never told anyone why.
theAuspiciousSeal.text: The first time this Order is placed in a slot, a die of the Magister is yours.
theAuspiciousSeal.note: Retired: the dice of the Magister are gone from the game, so this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theWarCouncil.name: The War Council
theWarCouncil.flavor: Three old soldiers, one map, and a great deal of shouting.
theWarCouncil.text: +2 combat strength for each military Order you have in a slot.

theGuildCharter.name: The Guild Charter
theGuildCharter.flavor: They asked for a seat at the table. They were given a page of it, and took the room.
theGuildCharter.text: +3 gold for each economic Order you have in a slot, and +2 production in your capital for each.

theSynod.name: The Synod
theSynod.flavor: Everyone speaks, nobody presides, and a decision is written down regardless.
theSynod.text: Your faith buildings give half again their yield, counted after every other share.
theSynod.note: A faith building is any building of yours that pays faith at all, and the share is taken last — after everything else that raised it.

theHarvestSongs.name: The Harvest Songs
theHarvestSongs.flavor: The reaping song is older than the field, and older than the kingdom.
theHarvestSongs.text: Every city gains 15% of its food yield again as culture.
theHarvestSongs.note: It reads the whole harvest rather than what is left after the citizens eat: a city's surplus is decided after every percentage on it, and a card that read the surplus would be reading a figure that reads the card back.

theSaltingHouses.name: The Salting Houses
theSaltingHouses.flavor: Salt keeps the fish, the fish keeps the town, and the town keeps the salt.
theSaltingHouses.text: Coastal cities gain 10% of their food yield again as production.
theSaltingHouses.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The Grain Fleet is the coast’s card now.

theDraftingHalls.name: The Drafting Halls
theDraftingHalls.flavor: Every beam is drawn twice: once for the builder, once for the book.
theDraftingHalls.text: Cities with a Library gain 20% of their production again as science.

theGoldenScales.name: The Golden Scales
theGoldenScales.flavor: What the counting-house learns about weight, the college learns about everything else.
theGoldenScales.text: Every city gains 20% of its gold yield again as science.

theArsenalLaw.name: The Arsenal Law
theArsenalLaw.flavor: In peace the yard is quiet. Nobody in it wants peace.
theArsenalLaw.text: While you are at war, cities with a Barracks gain 15% of their production again as gold.

theCharterOfTheMarches.name: The Charter of the Marches
theCharterOfTheMarches.flavor: The furthest town is written the widest liberties, and keeps them until it is no longer the furthest.
theCharterOfTheMarches.text: Your newest city gains +2 of every yield. Founding a city grants +30 culture.
theCharterOfTheMarches.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. It reads only at a founding, and the founding age ends.

theBalladWeavers.name: The Ballad-Weavers
theBalladWeavers.flavor: Every raider who falls in the passes is worth a verse, and the verses outlast the passes.
theBalladWeavers.text: +2 culture per turn for each barbarian you have killed while this Order stands in a slot.

theBellFounders.name: The Bell-Founders
theBellFounders.flavor: A rival raises a dome; the foundry answers with a bell, and the town agrees it is the finer sound.
theBellFounders.text: +1 culture per turn for each wonder finished anywhere in the world while this Order stands in a slot.
theBellFounders.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theReliquaryRolls.name: The Reliquary Rolls
theReliquaryRolls.flavor: They served, and then they were shelved: a knuckle, a brush, a name written large.
theReliquaryRolls.text: +3 faith and +3 culture per turn for each great person you have spent while this Order stands in a slot.

theChroniclersOfTheFallen.name: The Chroniclers of the Fallen
theChroniclersOfTheFallen.flavor: The roll of the dead is read aloud on market day, and the market is fuller for it.
theChroniclersOfTheFallen.text: +1 gold per turn for each unit you have lost in battle while this Order stands in a slot.

theAlmonersBook.name: The Almoners' Book
theAlmonersBook.flavor: What the treasury spends, the almoners write down; what the almoners write down, the schools read.
theAlmonersBook.text: +1 science per turn for each 400 gold you have spent buying while this Order stands in a slot.
theAlmonersBook.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. It paid less in a whole game than a single flat pays in a turn.

theCasusBelli.name: The Casus Belli
theCasusBelli.flavor: The grievance is old, the parchment is new, and the smiths were told a week ago.
theCasusBelli.text: Declaring war grants +4 combat strength to all your units and +10% production in every city, for 10 turns.

ritesCharter.name: The Rites Charter
ritesCharter.flavor: A room set aside, a lamp kept lit, and somewhere to put the singing.

vigilCharter.name: The Vigil Charter
vigilCharter.flavor: Somebody is awake. That is the whole of it.

scrivenersCharter.name: The Scriveners' Charter
scrivenersCharter.flavor: Nothing is known until it has been written out twice.

coinCharter.name: The Coin Charter
coinCharter.flavor: Weigh it, bite it, write it down, and only then agree.

waterwrightsCharter.name: The Waterwrights' Charter
waterwrightsCharter.flavor: A winter under the square is worth two rivers a day's walk away.

theSenatus.name: The Senatus
theSenatus.flavor: Everyone with something to lose, in one room, on the record.

toolmakersCharter.name: The Toolmakers' Charter
toolmakersCharter.flavor: First the tools, then the things the tools are for.

mintCharter.name: The Mint Charter
mintCharter.flavor: A face on the coin, and a song about the face.

stargazersCharter.name: The Stargazers' Charter
stargazersCharter.flavor: The sky is the one archive nobody has been able to edit.

justicesCharter.name: The Justices' Charter
justicesCharter.flavor: The circuit rides out twice a year, and the year is quieter for it.

theBannerCall.name: The Banner-Call
theBannerCall.flavor: Peace is the season in which the banners are mended.
theBannerCall.text: While you are at war: +15% production toward units, and killing a unit grants +5 culture.

theWolfStandard.name: The Wolf-Standard
theWolfStandard.flavor: The pole goes up where the camp came down.
theWolfStandard.text: Every barbarian camp you clear pays its bounty to all of your cities at once.
theWolfStandard.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theFarCharts.name: The Far Charts
theFarCharts.flavor: The edge of the sheet is only where the paper ran out.
theFarCharts.text: +1 science for each 20 hexes you have revealed.
theFarCharts.note: How far a caravan may be sent is settled by the two cities it joins and by the trading posts they have built. This law does not reach that rule.

theFoundingOath.name: The Founding Oath
theFoundingOath.flavor: The first stones were laid where the first oath was sworn.
theFoundingOath.text: Your capital pays +1 of every yield for each building standing in it, at most 3.
theFoundingOath.note: It counts the buildings standing in your capital rather than the first three ever raised there, and the third is the last that pays.

theLongRoads.name: The Long Roads
theLongRoads.flavor: The road is the realm. Everything else is where it stops.
theLongRoads.text: +1 gold for each road hex you have laid.
theLongRoads.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theRecklessLevy.name: The Reckless Levy
theRecklessLevy.flavor: Every man who can hold a spear, and some who cannot.
theRecklessLevy.text: +50% production toward units · every unit costs one more coin to keep.
theRecklessLevy.note: The coin is charged on each soldier the empire is already paying for, so a settler, a scout or a caravan is no dearer than it was.

theTitheOfIron.name: The Tithe of Iron
theTitheOfIron.flavor: The hill gives up its iron and the valley gives up its bread.
theTitheOfIron.text: +3 production on every mine · −3 food in every city with one.

breadAlone.name: Bread Alone
breadAlone.text: +3 food and −1 culture in every city.
breadAlone.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The Harvest Songs are the food deck’s card now.

theCongregation.name: The Congregation
theCongregation.flavor: Count the roofs that face your altar, not the ones that pay you.
theCongregation.text: +1 culture and +1 science for each city in the world that follows your religion.
theCongregation.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theGranaryLaws.name: The Granary Laws
theGranaryLaws.flavor: A full granary is an argument nobody wins.
theGranaryLaws.text: Cities of 8 or more population gain 20% of their food yield again as science.

theKingsRoad.name: The King's Road
theKingsRoad.flavor: The king's peace ends where the king's road does.
theKingsRoad.text: A unit that stops in one of your cities gets its movement back.
theKingsRoad.note: The realm's towns are stages on a march: a column that reaches one is fed, remounted and out of the gate the same day.

fieldHospitals.name: Field Hospitals
fieldHospitals.flavor: The wounded go back to the line. That is the whole of the art.
fieldHospitals.text: Units resting inside your own territory mend completely each turn.
fieldHospitals.note: A piece mends only where it rests: one that moved or struck this turn heals nothing, here or anywhere.

decisiveBlows.name: Decisive Blows
decisiveBlows.flavor: Wait for the stumble. Then do not wait.
decisiveBlows.text: +10 combat strength when attacking a unit below half strength.
decisiveBlows.note: A fight is decided by points on one ledger rather than by a share of the blow, so what was written as extra damage is printed as a strength line.

theMarshalsPurse.name: The Marshals' Purse
theMarshalsPurse.flavor: The treasury musters faster than the countryside.
theMarshalsPurse.text: Military units cost 25% less to buy.

knightlyOrders.name: Knightly Orders
knightlyOrders.flavor: They swore to the order first and to you second.
knightlyOrders.text: Mounted units gain +10 combat strength inside your territory, and cities put 25% less production behind them.

theSiegeTrain.name: The Siege Train
theSiegeTrain.flavor: The engines set out a week before the army does.
theSiegeTrain.text: Siege units gain +1 movement. +12 combat strength against cities for units standing beside a siege engine.

patrons.name: Patrons
patrons.flavor: The painter eats, and the city is remembered.
patrons.text: +10 culture for each wonder you hold. +3 renown per turn for each culture building you hold.

theGuildOfMasons.name: The Guild of Masons
theGuildOfMasons.flavor: One guild raises the cathedral. The armoury waits its turn.
theGuildOfMasons.text: +50% production toward wonders · −15% production toward units.

harbourmasters.name: Harbourmasters
harbourmasters.flavor: The harbour keeps its own hours and the city keeps to them.
harbourmasters.text: +1 trade route in every coastal city with a Harbour · +2 gold on every fishing boat.
harbourmasters.note: The harbour has to be built. A coastal town without one sends no more caravans than it did before.

theFactorHouses.name: The Factor Houses
theFactorHouses.flavor: A house in every port, and a ledger in every house.
theFactorHouses.text: +3 science for each trade route you run to another empire.
theFactorHouses.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. It paid less than a common card of a much earlier age.

assizeCourts.name: Assize Courts
assizeCourts.flavor: The judge rides a circuit, and the writ rides with him.
assizeCourts.text: +6 authority capacity · a captured city costs 1 authority.

theGrainFleet.name: The Grain Fleet
theGrainFleet.flavor: The corn comes in by water, and the water never tires.
theGrainFleet.text: +6 food in every coastal city · +1 gold for each 3 citizens in your coastal cities.

cathedralChapters.name: Cathedral Chapters
cathedralChapters.flavor: The chapter meets, and the town is quieter for a week.
cathedralChapters.text: +2 culture and +2 faith in every city with a Cathedral.

courtAstronomers.name: Court Astronomers
courtAstronomers.flavor: They read the sky the way a clerk reads a ledger.
courtAstronomers.text: +10 science for each wonder you hold.
courtAstronomers.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theConsistory.name: The Consistory
theConsistory.flavor: They meet under one roof and speak for every roof.
theConsistory.text: Your faith buildings pay double, counted after every other share.
theConsistory.note: A faith building is any building of yours that pays faith at all, and the doubling is taken last — after everything else that raised it.

scholastics.name: Scholastics
scholastics.flavor: Every question has an answer already. The trick is finding whose.
scholastics.text: +5 science for each University you hold · completing a technology grants +40 faith.

forcedMarch.name: Forced March
forcedMarch.flavor: Sleep is a thing that happens in your own country.
forcedMarch.text: Military units gain +1 movement outside your own territory.
forcedMarch.note: The march is quicker and costs nothing: nothing remembers how far a piece walked this turn.

admiralty.name: Admiralty
admiralty.text: Your units come ashore from the water without spending movement, and gain +10 combat strength for 3 turns when they land.
admiralty.note: A landing is the fleet's business, and the men who make one are still the fleet's for a few days afterwards.

theSalon.name: The Salon
theSalon.flavor: Everyone who matters is in one room, and they all want something.
theSalon.text: Every great person’s work pays double what it makes.
theSalon.note: The great-person improvements are the academy, landmark, manufactory, customs house and citadel.

theSilkExchange.name: The Silk Exchange
theSilkExchange.flavor: The bale is sold three times before it is unloaded.
theSilkExchange.text: +1 culture on every trade route you run, and your trade routes pay double science and culture.
theSilkExchange.note: The bale is sold three times before it is unloaded, and every sale is written down somewhere.

printingHouses.name: Printing Houses
printingHouses.flavor: The second copy costs nothing, which changes everything.
printingHouses.text: +3 culture for each Library you hold · +10% science in every city.

titheBarns.name: Tithe Barns
titheBarns.flavor: The barn belongs to the parish, and the parish belongs to the church.
titheBarns.text: Cities keep 50% of their stored food when they grow · −1 faith in every city.
titheBarns.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. It cost an empire more to hold than it ever paid back.

theGuildCompact.name: The Guild Compact
theGuildCompact.flavor: The guilds sign, and the price of everything is settled for a generation.
theGuildCompact.text: +3% production in a city for each production building standing in it, at most +15%.
theGuildCompact.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

manufactories.name: Manufactories
manufactories.flavor: One roof, a hundred hands, one thing made over and over.
manufactories.text: +30% production in every city with a manufactory inside its borders.
manufactories.note: One roof, a hundred hands, one thing made over and over — and the whole town builds faster for it.

theInquisition.name: The Inquisition
theInquisition.flavor: The questions are the same everywhere. So are the answers.
theInquisition.text: +8 faith and +8 culture in every city with a Temple.

universalSuffrage.name: Universal Suffrage
universalSuffrage.flavor: Everyone votes, and the ledger is read aloud.
universalSuffrage.text: +1 happiness for each 3 citizens in your empire · happiness tiers +10 percentage points.

theMagistersCourt.name: The Magister's Court
theMagistersCourt.flavor: The Magister keeps a court, and the court keeps the Work.
theMagistersCourt.note: The court doubles nothing yet: the fifth age has no great people in it, and no law can yet make a legacy count twice.
deferred: the legacies of great people of the fifth age count twice

theMusterRolls.name: The Muster Rolls
theMusterRolls.flavor: The first name on the list is read out twice.
theMusterRolls.text: The Order in your first military slot pays twice.

theHarvestHome.name: The Harvest Home
theHarvestHome.flavor: One sheaf more than anybody counted. Always.
theHarvestHome.text: Your Orders that give food give an additional food.

theReevesBell.name: The Reeve’s Bell
theReevesBell.flavor: It rings, and the granary doors stand open.
theReevesBell.text: Every 8 turns, your capital gains food for each citizen in your empire.

theFirstChair.name: The First Chair
theFirstChair.flavor: Nearest the fire, and twice as warm.
theFirstChair.text: The Order in your first economic slot pays twice.

theScriveners.name: The Scriveners
theScriveners.flavor: They copy everything, the margins included.
theScriveners.text: Your science buildings give half again their yield, the per-citizen lines included.

theSacredGround.name: The Sacred Ground
theSacredGround.flavor: Some hills were holy before anybody said so.
theSacredGround.text: +1 faith on every hex that already supplies faith.

theAssayersRule.name: The Assayer’s Rule
theAssayersRule.flavor: Every seam weighed, and weighed again.
theAssayersRule.text: +1 gold on every hex that already supplies gold.

theCountingHouses.name: The Counting Houses
theCountingHouses.flavor: The abacus has learned to lean upward.
theCountingHouses.text: Your gold buildings give half again their yield.

theAlmanacOfHours.name: The Almanac of Hours
theAlmanacOfHours.flavor: The feast comes sooner if you move the feast.
theAlmanacOfHours.text: Your Orders that pay every so many turns come round 3 turns sooner.

theFoundryDays.name: The Foundry Days
theFoundryDays.flavor: Ten days of smoke, and one of iron.
theFoundryDays.text: Every 10 turns, your capital gains production equal to half of what your empire makes in a turn.

theNetsBlessing.name: The Nets’ Blessing
theNetsBlessing.flavor: Bless the water and it fills the net twice.
theNetsBlessing.text: Every fishing boat pays double what it makes.

theHighChancery.name: The High Chancery
theHighChancery.flavor: Everything is worth more once it has reached the palace.
theHighChancery.text: Your Orders pay half again in your capital.

theVotiveTally.name: The Votive Tally
theVotiveTally.flavor: Ask the gods twice and they remember your face.
theVotiveTally.text: +1 faith for each Order draft you have asked again while this stands in a slot.
theVotiveTally.note: Only Order drafts you paid faith to see again are counted, and only while this sits in a chair. A doctrine, a name or a hand of gods asked again counts for nothing here.

theWorkshopsRule.name: The Workshops’ Rule
theWorkshopsRule.flavor: A hammer is worth what it strikes beside.
theWorkshopsRule.text: Your production buildings give half again their yield.

theWildChair.name: The Wild Chair
theWildChair.flavor: Nobody knows whose seat it is. Everybody sits in it.
theWildChair.text: The Order in your first wildcard slot pays twice.

theCantorsRule.name: The Cantors’ Rule
theCantorsRule.flavor: Sing the line again, and louder.
theCantorsRule.text: Your Orders that give faith give half again.

theGoldenCenser.name: The Golden Censer
theGoldenCenser.text: Every 15 turns, gain faith equal to half the science your empire makes in a turn.

theDeepSeams.name: The Deep Seams
theDeepSeams.flavor: Dig where the rock argues back.
theDeepSeams.text: Every mine pays double what it makes.

theExchangeCharter.name: The Exchange Charter
theExchangeCharter.flavor: Signed by everyone who could afford a pen.
theExchangeCharter.text: Your gold buildings give half again their yield, counted after every other share.

theTriumph.name: The Triumph
theTriumph.flavor: A parade is a city’s whole year spent in an afternoon.
theTriumph.text: Every 12 turns, gain culture equal to the production your empire makes in a turn.

theScholarsRule.name: The Scholars’ Rule
theScholarsRule.flavor: Every reading earns a second reading.
theScholarsRule.text: Your Orders that give science give an additional science.

theExchequer.name: The Exchequer
theExchequer.flavor: The road pays twice: once out, and once home.

theAssay.name: The Assay
theAssay.flavor: Melt the treasury down and see what it knew.
theAssay.text: Every 20 turns, gain science equal to the gold your empire makes in a turn.

theBroadAcres.name: The Broad Acres
theBroadAcres.flavor: Fields to the horizon, and behind the horizon, fields.
theBroadAcres.text: Every farm pays double what it makes.

theJubilee.name: The Jubilee
theJubilee.flavor: Debts forgiven, doors open, everybody singing.
theJubilee.text: Every 10 turns, gain faith for each citizen in your empire.
theJubilee.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theCompactOfChairs.name: The Compact of Chairs
theCompactOfChairs.flavor: Every seat at the head of its own table.
theCompactOfChairs.text: The Order in your first military, economic and wildcard slot each pay twice.

theLaureatesRule.name: The Laureates’ Rule
theLaureatesRule.flavor: One more verse. There is always one more verse.
theLaureatesRule.text: Your Orders that give culture give an additional culture.

theGreatClock.name: The Great Clock
theGreatClock.flavor: It runs fast, and it runs generous.
theGreatClock.text: Your Orders that pay every so many turns come round 3 turns sooner and pay half again.

theEncyclopaedists.name: The Encyclopaedists
theEncyclopaedists.flavor: They wrote everything down and it turned into song.
theEncyclopaedists.text: Every 10 turns, gain culture equal to the science your empire makes in a turn.

theCollegesRule.name: The Colleges’ Rule
theCollegesRule.flavor: Two lectures, one hall, twice the noise.
theCollegesRule.text: Your science buildings pay double, counted after every other share.

theGreatEnquiry.name: The Great Enquiry
theGreatEnquiry.text: The learning of the last age is counted toward the great work itself.
theGreatEnquiry.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theLastLaurels.name: The Last Laurels
theLastLaurels.flavor: Refuse the wreath and they carve you two.
theLastLaurels.text: A draft turned down is counted toward the great work itself.
theLastLaurels.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theSaltedEarth.name: The Salted Earth
theSaltedEarth.flavor: Nothing grows there now. That was the point.
theSaltedEarth.text: A city put to the torch is counted toward the great work itself.
theSaltedEarth.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theFinalProclamation.name: The Final Proclamation
theFinalProclamation.flavor: Read once, in every square, at the same hour.
theFinalProclamation.text: A prophet’s proclamation is counted toward the great work itself.
theFinalProclamation.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theEldersWrit.name: The Elders' Writ
theEldersWrit.flavor: The old men remember where every boundary stone was set.

theTallySticks.name: The Tally Sticks
theTallySticks.flavor: A notch for each debt, and a shelf of notches is a school.
theTallySticks.text: +1 science in every city with a Monument.

boatwrights.name: Boatwrights
boatwrights.flavor: Every village on the water keeps one man who knows what a keel is for.
boatwrights.note: A city counts as coastal when it stands on the water itself, not merely near it.

theMarches.name: The Marches
theMarches.flavor: The border is held by men who were promised the land beyond it.
theMarches.text: +2 authority capacity · −1 happiness in every city.

theCensus.name: The Census
theCensus.flavor: Every hearth counted, and every hearth answerable.
theCensus.text: +1 authority capacity for each 2 cities you hold.

theScribesHall.name: The Scribes' Hall
theScribesHall.flavor: A town grows large enough, and somebody starts writing things down.
theScribesHall.text: +1 science in every city for each 3 citizens living there.

theLampKeptLit.name: The Lamp Kept Lit
theLampKeptLit.flavor: One window in the palace burns all night, and has for a hundred years.

fishWeirs.name: Fish Weirs
fishWeirs.flavor: The tide brings them in twice a day and asks nothing back.
fishWeirs.note: The hex has to carry the boats already. Open water with nothing built on it pays no better.

tribute.name: Tribute
tribute.flavor: They keep their king. We keep the ledger.
tribute.text: +1 gold for each 2 citizens living in your puppets.
tribute.note: A puppet spends nothing of its own, so the coin is the realm's: annex the town and the tribute stops with the bowing.

ridersOfTheSteppe.name: Riders of the Steppe
ridersOfTheSteppe.flavor: A wall is a thing to ride around.
ridersOfTheSteppe.text: Mounted units ignore enemy zone of control and pillage without spending movement.
ridersOfTheSteppe.note: A raid still needs a horseman with something left to spend: what the law withholds is the point, not the price of admission.

tolls.name: Tolls
tolls.flavor: Every gate is a small customs house, and the realm has many gates.
tolls.text: +1 gold for each 4 road hexes you have laid.
tolls.note: It counts the paving your own workers laid, wherever the borders have since moved to.

mercenaries.name: Mercenaries
mercenaries.flavor: Loyalty by the season, and the season is paid in advance.
mercenaries.text: Newly created military units bought with gold gain +2 combat strength. All units cost 20% less to buy.
mercenaries.note: The blooding is written on the soldier at the moment the coin changes hands, and stays with them for life; a levy the countryside raised is a levy like any other.

theEntrepot.name: The Entrepôt
theEntrepot.flavor: The goods change hands twice on the quay, and pay duty each time.
theEntrepot.text: +1 gold for each 5 citizens in every city of yours that a foreign trade route ends in.
theEntrepot.note: It is the host that is paid, whoever sent the caravan: a road your own cities run between them pays nothing here.

patronage.name: Patronage
patronage.flavor: The city keeps the poets, and the poets keep the city.
patronage.text: +1 renown per turn for each 4 citizens in your capital.

pilgrims.name: Pilgrims
pilgrims.flavor: They walk because the road is the prayer.
pilgrims.text: Your capital carries its faith +6 hexes. +1 gold for each citizen of another empire who follows you.
pilgrims.note: The seat of a faith held itself and drifted nowhere until this: now the towns around your capital hear it too.
